cards.anchor: Produce three elevation samples with normalized attenuation spread at most 4 percent at second 120 in the stipulated water-and-dye exercise. One observed 300 rpm run met this proxy after stopping at second 60; repeated success and any time advantage over the preferred rule remain unproven.
cards.burden: Six fresh trials consume the full session allowance. Syringe substitution removes powered stirring but requires six timed manual transfers per migration trial, rinsing, reference checks, optical logging and depth sampling. Reduced stirring seconds do not establish reduced operator effort or energy use.
cards.construction: Run two triplets: fixed rotation, syringe migration, then carrier-removal attack; reverse arm order in triplet two. Each trial uses 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye in the rinsed beaker, the same bottle, fixed addition location, locked camera and spill tray. Rotation commands 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds. Migration keeps the stirrer off and uses six needle-free 20 mL low-position withdrawals and upper-side returns, completed at seconds 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 with fixed marked positions. Attack uses zero transfers and zero stirring. Stop active operations at second 60 independently of optical spread; never restart. Record five-second images without feedback. At second 120 withdraw 1 mL from each marked depth within ten seconds, alternating depth order across trials. Apply water and common-aliquot references per block; report raw vial readings, spread, duration, transfer counts and every failure. Stop if liquid escapes.
cards.defeat: Repeated migration spread above 4 percent while matched fixed-rotation controls meet the target defeats this specified substitution. Migration and attack both passing fails to support the claimed transfer contribution. Both failing, inconsistent separation, or failures of reference checks leave the proposed mechanism unresolved and do not establish preferred-rule necessity.
cards.mutation: Hypothesis: migrate dye redistribution from continuous rotation and its optical stop interface to a fixed count of low-to-high bulk transfers; then remove that new carrier in a separate zero-transfer arm to test whether the outcome actually depends on it.
cards.prediction_candidate: If the transfer carrier contributes enough redistribution, migration will meet the at-most-4-percent vial target in both triplets while zero-transfer attack exceeds it. Fixed rotation is an observed-success comparator whose repeat success remains a hypothesis. Replicated separation would support transfer contribution within this recipe without proving unique necessity.
cards.prediction_rival: If passive redistribution or sampling-mediated equalization suffices, both migration and zero-transfer attack will meet the target; depth-order dependence may expose sampling effects. Such results would undermine the transfer-specific explanation even if migration appears successful.
cards.probe: Compare second-120 vial spread for migration versus zero-transfer attack within each triplet, with fixed 300 rpm as the bounded control. Match operation cutoff and quiet interval, reverse arm order and alternate sampling order. Require the same direction of migration/attack separation in both triplets, reporting individual results rather than selecting successes. Side-image stability is neither a stop command nor the outcome criterion.
cards.rival: Hypothesis: the apparent uniformity can arise through passive transport or disturbed sampling without a causally useful transfer carrier. Transfer geometry may also be inadequate, so migration failure alone cannot favor sustained 900 rpm or its optical rule.
unknowns: Transfer success and repeated lower-speed success are unobserved; two trials per arm provide limited replication.
Sampling and transfers can disturb gradients; alternating sample order cannot eliminate that uncertainty.
Attenuation repeatability is not concentration calibration, and the nominal speed lacks independent verification.
Matched 900 rpm final readings and its total stirring duration are absent, limiting relative performance claims.
Speck identity and the proposed optical return loop remain unresolved; this probe does not identify either.
Results cannot establish performance for other viscosities, solutes, vessel sizes or continuous processes, or real chemical or human benefit.
